In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel bone-targeted agents that are designed to inhibit the growth of bone metastases, while minimizing the risk of osteonecrosis of the jaw.
the study of a new type of bone turnover marker (BTM), which are proteins that reflect the bone remodeling process, and their role as predictive factors in breast cancer and bone disease.
the development of novel methods for the analysis of complex data sets in the context of bone metastases and bone turnover.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

bisphosphonate treatment is effective in reducing the incidence of bone metastases and in reducing bone-related pain, skeletal-related events, and bone resorption markers in patients with breast or prostate cancer.

the use of bone turnover markers is not a substitute for the clinical assessment of the patient, but it can be a valuable tool in clinical practice to monitor patients treated with anti-resorptive agents.

bisphosphonate therapy is not associated with a reduced risk of fracture in patients with osteoporosis and is associated with a reduced incidence of vertebral and non-vertebral fractures in patients with osteopenia or osteoporosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ZOMAR study showed that the use of bone turnover markers in the clinical management of patients with breast cancer bone metastases treated by bisphosphonate therapy is feasible, but that their clinical utility is still limited.

the ZOMAR study has demonstrated the usefulness of bone turnover markers as a tool for the evaluation of the efficacy of bisphosphonate treatment in patients with breast and prostate cancer and bone metastasis.
we have identified several novel genes and gene variants associated with bone mineral density and osteoporosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bone turnover markers are not a good indicator of bone metastasis development in breast cancer.
bone turnover markers are useful to identify patients with bone metastases who will benefit from bisphosphonate treatment.
bone turnover markers can help us identify women with early stage breast cancer who are at high risk of developing bone metastasis and who may therefore benefit from bisphosphonate therapy.
